paragraphs.text: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit,
paragraphs.original: Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ,
paragraphs.translit: Alētheian legō en Christō, ou pseudomai, symmartyrousēs moi tēs syneidēseōs mou en pneumati hagiō,

paragraphs.text: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι λύπη μοί ἐστιν μεγάλη καὶ ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη τῇ καρδίᾳ μου·
paragraphs.translit: hoti lypē moi estin megalē kai adialeiptos odynē tē kardia mou·

paragraphs.text: For I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren`s sake, my kinsmen according to the flesh:
paragraphs.original: ηὐχόμην γὰρ ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν συγγενῶν μου κατὰ σάρκα,
paragraphs.translit: ēuchomēn gar anathema einai autos egō apo tou Christou hyper tōn adelphōn mou tōn syngenōn mou kata sarka,

paragraphs.text: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service [of God], and the promises;
paragraphs.original: οἵτινές εἰσιν Ἰσραηλῖται, ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι,
paragraphs.translit: hoitines eisin Israēlitai, hōn hē hyiothesia kai hē doxa kai hai diathēkai kai hē nomothesia kai hē latreia kai hai epangeliai,

paragraphs.text: whose are the fathers, and of whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.
paragraphs.original: ὧν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ ἐξ ὧν ὁ χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ ὢν ἐπὶ πάντων, θεὸς εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
paragraphs.translit: hōn hoi pateres, kai ex hōn ho christos to kata sarka, ho ōn epi pantōn, theos eulogētos eis tous aiōnas· amēn.

paragraphs.text: But [it is] not as though the word of God hath come to nought. For they are not all Israel, that are of Israel:
paragraphs.original: Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ. οὐ γὰρ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ, οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ·
paragraphs.translit: Ouch hoion de hoti ekpeptōken ho logos tou theou. ou gar pantes hoi ex Israēl, houtoi Israēl·

paragraphs.text: neither, because they are Abraham`s seed, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.
paragraphs.original: οὐδʼ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, πάντες τέκνα, ἀλλʼ· Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα.
paragraphs.translit: oudʼ hoti eisin sperma Abraam, pantes tekna, allʼ· En Isaak klēthēsetai soi sperma.

paragraphs.text: That is, it is not the children of the flesh that are children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned for a seed.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτʼ ἔστιν, οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς ταῦτα τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα·
paragraphs.translit: toutʼ estin, ou ta tekna tēs sarkos tauta tekna tou theou, alla ta tekna tēs epangelias logizetai eis sperma·

paragraphs.text: For this is a word of promise, According to this season will I come, and Sarah shall have a son.
paragraphs.original: ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος· Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός.
paragraphs.translit: epangelias gar ho logos houtos· Kata ton kairon touton eleusomai kai estai tē Sarra hyios.

paragraphs.text: And not only so; but Rebecca also having conceived by one, [even] by our father Isaac--
paragraphs.original: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα, Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: ou monon de, alla kai Rhebekka ex henos koitēn echousa, Isaak tou patros hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: for [the children] being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth,
paragraphs.original: μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ φαῦλον, ἵνα ἡ κατʼ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις τοῦ θεοῦ μένῃ,
paragraphs.translit: mēpō gar gennēthentōn mēde praxantōn ti agathon ē phaulon, hina hē katʼ eklogēn prothesis tou theou menē,

paragraphs.text: it was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ ὅτι Ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι·
paragraphs.translit: ouk ex ergōn allʼ ek tou kalountos, errethē autē hoti Ho meizōn douleusei tō elassoni·

paragraphs.text: Even as it is written, Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gegraptai· Ton Iakōb ēgapēsa, ton de Ēsau emisēsa.

paragraphs.text: What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ; μὴ γένοιτο·
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun eroumen; mē adikia para tō theō; mē genoito·

paragraphs.text: For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.
paragraphs.original: τῷ Μωϋσεῖ γὰρ λέγει· Ἐλεήσω ὃν ἂν ἐλεῶ, καὶ οἰκτιρήσω ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω.
paragraphs.translit: tō Mōysei gar legei· Eleēsō hon an eleō, kai oiktirēsō hon an oiktirō.

paragraphs.text: So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that hath mercy.
paragraphs.original: ἄρα οὖν οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ara oun ou tou thelontos oude tou trechontos alla tou eleōntos theou.

paragraphs.text: For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, For this very purpose did I raise thee up, that I might show in thee my power, and that my name might be published abroad in all the earth.
paragraphs.original: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῷ Φαραὼ ὅτι Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐξήγειρά σε ὅπως ἐνδείξωμαι ἐν σοὶ τὴν δύναμίν μου, καὶ ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.
paragraphs.translit: legei gar hē graphē tō Pharaō hoti Eis auto touto exēgeira se hopōs endeixōmai en soi tēn dynamin mou, kai hopōs diangelē to onoma mou en pasē tē gē.

paragraphs.text: So then he hath mercy on whom he will, and whom he will be hardeneth.
paragraphs.original: ἄρα οὖν ὃν θέλει ἐλεεῖ, ὃν δὲ θέλει σκληρύνει.
paragraphs.translit: ara oun hon thelei eleei, hon de thelei sklērynei.

paragraphs.text: Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he still find fault? For who withstandeth his will?
paragraphs.original: Ἐρεῖς μοι οὖν· Τί οὖν ἔτι μέμφεται; τῷ γὰρ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνθέστηκεν;
paragraphs.translit: Ereis moi oun· Ti oun eti memphetai; tō gar boulēmati autou tis anthestēken;

paragraphs.text: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why didst thou make me thus?
paragraphs.original: ὦ ἄνθρωπε, μενοῦνγε σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ ἀνταποκρινόμενος τῷ θεῷ; μὴ ἐρεῖ τὸ πλάσμα τῷ πλάσαντι Τί με ἐποίησας οὕτως;
paragraphs.translit: ō anthrōpe, menounge sy tis ei ho antapokrinomenos tō theō; mē erei to plasma tō plasanti Ti me epoiēsas houtōs;

paragraphs.text: Or hath not the potter a right over the clay, from the same lump to make one part a vessel unto honor, and another unto dishonor?
paragraphs.original: ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τοῦ πηλοῦ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν;
paragraphs.translit: ē ouk echei exousian ho kerameus tou pēlou ek tou autou phyramatos poiēsai ho men eis timēn skeuos ho de eis atimian;

paragraphs.text: What if God, willing to show his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering vessels of wrath fitted unto destruction:
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ θέλων ὁ θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν,
paragraphs.translit: ei de thelōn ho theos endeixasthai tēn orgēn kai gnōrisai to dynaton autou ēnenken en pollē makrothymia skeuē orgēs katērtismena eis apōleian,

paragraphs.text: and that he might make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he afore prepared unto glory,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους, ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai hina gnōrisē ton plouton tēs doxēs autou epi skeuē eleous, ha proētoimasen eis doxan,

paragraphs.text: [even] us, whom he also called, not from the Jews only, but also from the Gentiles?
paragraphs.original: οὓς καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν;—
paragraphs.translit: hous kai ekalesen hēmas ou monon ex Ioudaiōn alla kai ex ethnōn;—

paragraphs.text: As he saith also in Hosea, I will call that my people, which was not my people; And her beloved, that was not beloved.
paragraphs.original: ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει· Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου καὶ τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην·
paragraphs.translit: hōs kai en tō Hōsēe legei· Kalesō ton ou laon mou laon mou kai tēn ouk ēgapēmenēn ēgapēmenēn·

paragraphs.text: And it shall be, [that] in the place where it was said       unto them, Ye are not my people, There shall they be called sons of the living God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς· Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.
paragraphs.translit: kai estai en tō topō hou errethē autois· Ou laos mou hymeis, ekei klēthēsontai hyioi theou zōntos.

paragraphs.text: And Isaiah crieth concerning Israel, If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, it is the remnant that shall be saved:
paragraphs.original: Ἠσαΐας δὲ κράζει ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ· Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸ ὑπόλειμμα σωθήσεται·
paragraphs.translit: Ēsaias de krazei hyper tou Israēl· Ean ē ho arithmos tōn hyiōn Israēl hōs hē ammos tēs thalassēs, to hypoleimma sōthēsetai·

paragraphs.text: for the Lord will execute [his] word upon the earth, finishing it and cutting it short.
paragraphs.original: λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: logon gar syntelōn kai syntemnōn poiēsei kyrios epi tēs gēs.

paragraphs.text: And, as Isaiah hath said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, We had become as Sodom, and had been made like unto Gomorrah.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθὼς προείρηκεν Ἠσαΐας· Εἰ μὴ κύριος Σαβαὼθ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἡμῖν σπέρμα, ὡς Σόδομα ἂν ἐγενήθημεν καὶ ὡς Γόμορρα ἂν ὡμοιώθημεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai kathōs proeirēken Ēsaias· Ei mē kyrios Sabaōth enkatelipen hēmin sperma, hōs Sodoma an egenēthēmen kai hōs Gomorra an hōmoiōthēmen.

paragraphs.text: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, who followed not after righteousness, attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith:
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὅτι ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην κατέλαβεν δικαιοσύνην, δικαιοσύνην δὲ τὴν ἐκ πίστεως·
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun eroumen; hoti ethnē ta mē diōkonta dikaiosynēn katelaben dikaiosynēn, dikaiosynēn de tēn ek pisteōs·

paragraphs.text: but Israel, following after a law of righteousness, did not arrive at [that] law.
paragraphs.original: Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης εἰς νόμον οὐκ ἔφθασεν.
paragraphs.translit: Israēl de diōkōn nomon dikaiosynēs eis nomon ouk ephthasen.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore? Because [they sought it] not by faith, but as it were by works. They stumbled at the stone of stumbling;
paragraphs.original: διὰ τί; ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐξ ἔργων· προσέκοψαν τῷ λίθῳ τοῦ προσκόμματος,
paragraphs.translit: dia ti; hoti ouk ek pisteōs allʼ hōs ex ergōn· prosekopsan tō lithō tou proskommatos,

paragraphs.text: even as it is written, Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence: And he that believeth on him shall not be put to shame.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gegraptai· Idou tithēmi en Siōn lithon proskommatos kai petran skandalou, kai ho pisteuōn epʼ autō ou kataischynthēsetai.
